result.output:
Exit codes: `0` success or no-op, `1` failure, `2` usage, `127` a required
binary is missing, `130` interrupted. A non-empty diff is not a failure.

### What the overlay records

Alongside the digest, the overlay carries two annotations in
`commonAnnotations`:

```yaml
commonAnnotations:
  deploy.internal/source-commit: 197a3ae981068c375be77cb03e8c85e5ce304612
  deploy.internal/release: 1.4.2
```

`deploy.internal/release` is present only when the digests came from a release,
and a deploy of the current commit **removes** it — a version left beside an
unrelated digest would be read as fact by `deploy promote`, which would then
promote a version that environment never ran. It exists because promotion copies
digests, and a digest does not say which release it belongs to; without it a
promotion could not report `prod 1.4.1 → 1.4.2`.

kustomize propagates common annotations onto pod templates, so a deploy whose
digest is unchanged but whose commit moved still restarts the pods. That is
deliberate — an annotation named `source-commit` that did not track the source
commit would be worse — and the plan says so explicitly when it is the only
change.

## Confirming what is deployed (`intropy deploy status`)

The last step of the release process is checking that the same thing really is
running everywhere:

```sh
intropy deploy status order-extractor
```

```
COMPONENT        ENV      RELEASE  DIGEST               AGE  SYNC    HEALTH
order-extractor  dev      1.4.2    sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc  2h   Synced  Healthy
order-extractor  staging  1.4.2    sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc  47m  Synced  Healthy
order-extractor  prod     1.4.2    sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc  3m   Synced  Healthy

all 3 environments run sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc — these are the same bits, promoted rather than rebuilt
```

The identical digest in every row is the whole point of the design. Promotion
copies digests rather than rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes
"production runs the bits staging tested" a fact instead of a hope — and the
line under the table says whether it holds, so nobody has to compare three
truncated hashes by eye.

When it does not hold, the environments are grouped by what they actually run:

```
the environments do not all run the same bits: dev runs sha256:abc123abc123; staging and prod run sha256:ad22d6f2ecbc
```

Rows are ordered by the promotion graph in `deploy.yaml`, not alphabetically, so
the last row is the furthest downstream. Only the environments the component
declares are shown.

Where each column comes from:

| Column | Source |
| --- | --- |
| `RELEASE` | the overlay's `deploy.internal/release` annotation, or `@<short sha>` from `deploy.internal/source-commit` when it was deployed from a commit |
| `DIGEST` | the digest the overlay pins, in the same form `deploy` and `promote` print |
| `AGE` | the commit that last changed that overlay — ArgoCD reports no timestamp, and the commit is when the change reached the branch |
| `SYNC`, `HEALTH` | ArgoCD's `status.sync.status` and `status.health.status` |

**Nothing here can fail on one bad environment.** An overlay that pins a tag, an
environment the component has never been deployed to, an application ArgoCD does
not know — each is reported as a note under the table and the other rows still
print, because the point of the table is the environments that are fine next to
the one that is not. This is the opposite of `deploy promote`, which *refuses* to
copy out of a tag-pinned overlay; describing one is not the same as promoting it.

If ArgoCD cannot be reached at all, `SYNC` and `HEALTH` are left empty and
everything else still prints with a warning on stderr. Those two columns are the
only ones that come from the cluster; withholding the digests over them would be
withholding most of the answer over part of it.

An environment whose overlay has a committed change ArgoCD has not applied is
called out with the command to review it — for a `sync: manual` environment that
is the normal resting state of an unspent gate, not a fault:

```
prod has a committed change ArgoCD has not applied, waiting on its manual sync gate:
  intropy deploy diff order-extractor --env prod
```

The exit code is **always 0**, even when the environments disagree. This reports;
it does not gate. To gate in CI, read `consistent` from the machine-readable
form, which also carries every image rather than just the one the table has room
for, and the deploy time as an instant rather than a rendered age:

```sh
intropy deploy status order-extractor --output json | jq -e '.consistent'
```

Nothing is written to git, no sync is triggered, `kubectl` is never invoked, and
`kustomize` is not required.

## Releases (`intropy release`)

A release gives the images built for one source commit a durable version. It
**does not deploy or change any environment**.

### What happens

For `intropy release create component-x --version 1.4.2`, the CLI:

1. Verifies that `git` is available, then locks and refreshes its cached GitOps
   checkout to find `component-x` and read its source paths and images.
2. Checks that the relevant source paths are clean and that the commit to
   release is pushed. The commit is `HEAD` by default; `--ref` selects another
   pushed revision.
3. Resolves the exact image digests CI built for that commit and generates notes
   from the component-scoped commits since the closest ancestor release, or from
   the explicit `--since` baseline.
4. Publishes a versioned OCI release manifest containing the component, source
   commit, image digests, notes, and their comparison basis. It does not update
   any GitOps overlay.
5. Creates and pushes the annotated Git tag `component-x/v1.4.2`. A tag-push
   failure is a warning because the OCI manifest is the release; re-running can
   repair a missing tag.

Re-running for a version that already exists compares the intended manifest to
the published one. An identical release is left in place and a missing Git tag
is repaired; a different release is refused because versions are immutable.

Inspect a published release before shipping it:

```sh
intropy release view component-x 1.4.2
```

This command changes no source repository, GitOps remote, or environment. It
refreshes the local GitOps cache to locate component metadata, then resolves
that version's OCI manifest and prints its source commit, image digests,
comparison basis, and generated notes. Use `-o json` to receive the manifest
itself. It verifies that the requested OCI tag and the manifest's declared
version agree.

Ship the inspected release with
`intropy deploy <component> <version> --env <env>`.

## Onboarding a system (`intropy deploy init`)

Every command below assumes the component already exists in the GitOps
repository. Getting it there used to be manual — hand-writing
`component.yaml`, `base/` and an overlay per environment, for every block, in
every customer repository. `deploy init` generates that tree from the topology
the system host declares:

```sh
# from a system workspace
intropy deploy init --plan
```

Everything the CLI can derive is filled in: each block's workload (an extractor
is a `CronJob`, everything else a `Deployment`), the app-ids that belong in a
Dapr component's `scopes:`, the environments `deploy.yaml` defines, the
registry. What it cannot derive — connection strings, hosts, credentials, cron
schedules — is emitted as a `REPLACE-ME-<HINT>` placeholder and listed when the
run finishes. Filling those in is the remaining job.

Image tags are never in that list. Scaffolding leaves them at an `unpinned`
sentinel, because pinning digests is `intropy deploy`'s job and nothing else's.

The system's shared objects — the Dapr pub/sub and secret store its blocks
resolve by name, plus the secrets behind them — go in a `host` directory of
their own, declared `kind: shared` in `component.yaml`:

```
domains/sales/ordersync/
  host/                    kind: shared — no image, nothing to pin
    base/dapr/pubsub.yaml  one owner, scopes: limits who may use it
    base/secrets/
  order-extract/           extractor ⇒ CronJob
  order-load/              loader ⇒ Deployment
```

A Dapr `Component` is namespace-scoped and every integration in the namespace
shares it, so exactly one ArgoCD Application may own each one. The `host`
directory is what gives them that owner; `scopes:` is what limits who may use
them. `deploy` and `promote` refuse a `kind: shared` component, since it has no
image to pin.

Which Dapr components get rendered depends on the platform, declared once per
repository in `deploy.yaml`:

```yaml
platform:
  provider: beebyte      # azure, beebyte, …
  pubsub: rabbitmq       # in-memory, rabbitmq, servicebus, …
  secretStore: kubernetes
```

The CLI itself knows nothing about any of those values: the string flows from
`deploy.yaml` into a template parameter and into a `spec.files` condition in the
template library, so adding a platform is a templates-repo change. The
components live in `base/` and are identical in every environment — what varies
per environment is the credential, which a Dapr component reaches through
`secretKeyRef`.

Nothing is pushed to the default branch; a tree full of placeholders would be
picked up by the ApplicationSet immediately. The run pushes
`deploy-init/<domain>-<system>` for review. Re-running is additive: a file that
already exists and differs is reported and left alone unless `--force` is given,
and `--force` still refuses to overwrite an overlay that pins a digest.

### Where the system lands

The GitOps path is `domains/<domain>/<system>/<component>/`, and both segments
are derived rather than typed:

- **`<system>`** comes from the topology record. Pass `--system` when the
  workspace holds several — see below.
- **`<domain>`** comes from where the system already sits in the GitOps tree; on
  a first run, from the workspace's own `domains/<domain>/<system>/` layout,
  which every integrations tree mirrors from the deployment tree. `--domain`
  overrides both, and is only *required* when the workspace has some other
  shape.

If the two disagree — the repository files a system under one domain and the
workspace suggests another — the repository wins and the run says so. Moving a
system between domains should be deliberate, not a side effect of a directory
name.

### Picking a system

An integrations tree usually holds several systems side by side, so `--system`
says which one:

```sh
intropy deploy init --system order-flow
```

The name is matched against each scaffolded host's recorded system name and its
system directory — both already on disk — so picking a system never builds the
others. `OrderFlow` and `order-flow` are the same system, matching how
`intropy sys create` kebab-cases what you give it. With one system in the
workspace the flag is unnecessary; with several and no `--system`, the command
lists them and stops rather than guessing.

`--system` also names the tree segment. If it differs from what the topology
declares, your name wins and the run says so.

The topology comes from the host's `graph` verb, which builds the project first.
In CI, capture it once and skip the build:

```sh
dotnet run --project ./OrderSync.SystemHost -- graph > topology.json

```

The manifests come from the template library's latest release. `--version` pins
a tag instead — the same flag `intropy int create` uses, and the one that makes
a re-run reproducible while the templates are still moving:

```sh
intropy deploy init --version v0.4.0
```

The resolved tag is echoed as it fetches and recorded as `template` in
`--output json`, so a reviewer of the pushed branch can tell which release
produced the tree.

## Deployment (`intropy deploy`)

Pin the image digest that CI built for your current commit into one
environment's kustomize overlay in the GitOps repository.

Run it inside the component's source repository:

```sh
intropy deploy order-extractor --env dev --plan
```

`--plan` renders the overlay before and after the change and prints a diff
without writing anything. Drop it to commit and push:

```sh
intropy deploy order-extractor --env dev
```

That stages only the overlay's `kustomization.yaml`, commits it with trailers
recording what was deployed, and pushes to the GitOps repository's default
branch.

To ship a published release rather than the current commit, pass its version:

```sh
intropy deploy order-extractor 1.4.2 --env staging
```

The release manifest already records the digests, so nothing reads the source
repository — no `HEAD`, no cleanliness check, no registry tag lookup — and the
command works from any directory. Everything after that is identical: the same
plan, diff, commit, push and ArgoCD wait. If someone else pushed first the push is rejected, and the commit is
rebased onto their work and retried — up to five times, with jittered backoff.

A rebase *conflict* means someone deployed the same component to the same
environment in the same moment. That fails loudly and pushes nothing:
auto-resolving would silently pick a winner and discard a deployment someone
believes succeeded. Re-run to deploy on top of theirs.

### What happens

For `intropy deploy order-extractor --env dev`, the CLI:

1. Verifies that `git` and `kustomize` are available and resolves the GitOps
   repository from the flag, environment, or user configuration.
2. Locks and refreshes its cached local GitOps checkout, so two local deploys
   cannot edit, reset, or revert the same checkout concurrently.
3. Reads the `dev` and `order-extractor` metadata, then checks that the current
   source checkout is clean for that component and that `HEAD` was pushed. With
   a version given, both checks are skipped: the release already recorded what
   was built, so there is no working tree to vet.
4. Resolves the image digest CI published for that commit — or reads the digests
   the release recorded — temporarily updates the Kustomize overlay, renders it
   before and after, and verifies that the requested image pin reached the
   rendered manifests.
5. With `--plan`, prints the diff and reverts the temporary edit. Without it,
   commits only the changed `kustomization.yaml` and pushes that commit to the
   GitOps repository's default branch.

After pushing, deploy waits for ArgoCD to apply the new revision and become
healthy. `--no-wait` skips it and `--timeout` bounds it (default 5m).

For an environment with `sync: manual`, deploy commits and stops without
waiting — the gate is in ArgoCD, so it prints the `deploy diff` and `deploy sync`
follow-up, with the revision to review, rather than waiting for a sync that will
never start on its own.

164		}

166			m.Component != other.Component ||
167			m.Version != other.Version ||
168			m.Source != other.Source ||
169			m.Notes != other.Notes ||
170			m.ChangeBasis != other.ChangeBasis {

175		}
176		for i := range m.Images {

33		Environment string `json:"environment"`
34		Status      string `json:"status"`

37		// same form as Plan.Previous. A missing key means the overlay has no entry

39		Pinned map[string]string `json:"pinned,omitempty"`

46	// InspectUpstreams reads what each environment named by the target's
47	// promotesFrom currently has pinned, and compares it with the digests about to
48	// be deployed.
49	//
50	// Informational, and deliberately so: promotion policy — refusing a staging
51	// deploy of bits dev never ran, honouring requireSourceHealthy — belongs to the
52	// promote command. A deploy that *says* "these are not the bits dev tested" is
53	// more useful than one that refuses to run.
54	//
55	// Nothing here can fail. An environment with no overlay for this component, an
56	// unreadable kustomization, or the target naming itself yields a note or
57	// nothing at all.
58	func InspectUpstreams(root string, coord gitops.Coordinate, comp *gitops.ComponentConfig, target string, env gitops.EnvironmentConfig, pins []source.Pin) []Upstream {
59		var out []Upstream
60		for _, name := range env.PromotesFrom {
61			// An environment that promotes from itself would compare the overlay
62			// with the edit about to be made to it. deploy.yaml does not forbid it.
63			if name == target {
64				continue
65			}
66			out = append(out, inspectUpstream(root, coord, comp, name, pins))
67		}
68		return out
69	}

71	func inspectUpstream(root string, coord gitops.Coordinate, comp *gitops.ComponentConfig, upstream string, pins []source.Pin) Upstream {
72		u := Upstream{Environment: upstream, Status: UpstreamUnknown}
73	
74		dir, err := gitops.ResolveOverlay(root, coord, comp, upstream)
75		if err != nil {
76			return u
77		}
78		k, _, err := kustomize.ReadKustomization(dir)
79		if err != nil {
80			return u
81		}
82	
83		u.SourceCommit = k.CommonAnnotations[kustomize.AnnotationSourceCommit]
84		u.Pinned = make(map[string]string, len(pins))
85	
86		status := UpstreamMatch
87		for _, pin := range pins {
88			img, found := k.FindImage(pin.Image)
89			if !found || img.Digest == "" {
90				if found {
91					u.Pinned[pin.Image] = img.Pinned()
92				}
93				// Unpinned outranks differs: "there is nothing to compare" is the
94				// more accurate thing to say about the whole environment.
95				status = UpstreamUnpinned
96				break
97			}
98			u.Pinned[pin.Image] = img.Digest
99			if img.Digest != pin.Digest {
100				status = UpstreamDiffers
101			}
102		}
103		u.Status = status
104		return u
105	}
106	
107	// Describe renders the one-line reassurance, or the one-line qualification.
108	func (u Upstream) Describe(pins []source.Pin) string {
109		switch u.Status {
110		case UpstreamMatch:
111			subject := "these digests"
112			if len(pins) == 1 {
113				subject = "this digest"
114			}
115			if u.SourceCommit != "" {
116				return fmt.Sprintf("%s already runs %s (commit %s) — you are shipping the tested bits",
117					u.Environment, subject, git.ShortSHA(u.SourceCommit))
118			}
119			return fmt.Sprintf("%s already runs %s — you are shipping the tested bits", u.Environment, subject)
120	
121		case UpstreamDiffers:
122			image, digest := u.firstDisagreement(pins)
123			return fmt.Sprintf("%s runs a different digest for %s (%s) — these bits have not run there",
124				u.Environment, image, shortDigest(digest))
125	
126		case UpstreamUnpinned:
127			image, _ := u.firstDisagreement(pins)
128			return fmt.Sprintf("%s pins no digest for %s, so there is nothing to compare", u.Environment, image)
129	
130		default:
131			return fmt.Sprintf("%s could not be read, so there is nothing to compare", u.Environment)
132		}
133	}
134	
135	// firstDisagreement names the first image, in declared order, that the upstream
136	// environment does not pin to the digest being deployed. Declared order keeps
137	// the message stable across runs.
138	func (u Upstream) firstDisagreement(pins []source.Pin) (image, digest string) {
139		for _, pin := range pins {
140			there, found := u.Pinned[pin.Image]
141			if !found || there != pin.Digest {
142				return pin.Image, there
143			}
144		}
145		// Unreachable for differs and unpinned, but a plausible message beats an
146		// empty one if a caller ever asks about a match.
147		if len(pins) > 0 {
148			return pins[0].Image, u.Pinned[pins[0].Image]
149		}
150		return "", ""
151	}

9	import (

14		"net"

16		"os"
17		"time"
18	)

20	// Options configures a dashboard server. The zero value is not usable; Root is
21	// required and Addr/Port select the listen address.
22	type Options struct {
23		// Root is the workspace directory scanned for integrations.
24		Root string
25		// Addr is the host/interface to bind, e.g. "127.0.0.1". Empty binds all.
26		Addr string
27		// Port is the TCP port to bind. 0 asks the OS for a free port.
28		Port int

30		OpenBrowser bool
31		// Version is reported by GET /api/health.
32		Version string
33		// Stdout and Stderr receive program output and diagnostics; both default
34		// to the process streams when nil.
35		Stdout io.Writer
36		Stderr io.Writer
37	}
38	
39	// shutdownTimeout bounds how long in-flight requests have to drain on Ctrl+C.
40	const shutdownTimeout = 5 * time.Second
41	
42	// Serve starts the dashboard and blocks until ctx is cancelled (e.g. SIGINT)
43	// or the server fails. On cancellation it shuts down gracefully and returns
44	// nil; it returns a non-nil error only for a real startup or runtime failure.
45	func Serve(ctx context.Context, opts Options) error {
46		if opts.Stdout == nil {
47			opts.Stdout = os.Stdout
48		}
49		if opts.Stderr == nil {
50			opts.Stderr = os.Stderr
51		}
52		root := opts.Root
53		if root == "" {
54			root = "."
55		}
56	
57		handler, err := newHandler(root, opts.Version, hostGraphProvider(root))
58		if err != nil {
59			return fmt.Errorf("run: %w", err)
60		}
61	
62		addr := net.JoinHostPort(opts.Addr, fmt.Sprintf("%d", opts.Port))
63		ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", addr)
64		if err != nil {
65			return fmt.Errorf("run: cannot listen on %s: %w", addr, err)
66		}
67	
68		url := displayURL(opts.Addr, ln.Addr())
69		fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "Intropy dashboard running at %s\n", url)
70		fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stderr, "Press Ctrl+C to stop.")
71	
72		if opts.OpenBrowser {
73			if err := openBrowser(url); err != nil {
74				fmt.Fprintf(opts.Stderr, "warning: could not open browser: %v\n", err)
75			}
76		}
77	
78		srv := &http.Server{Handler: handler}
79		errCh := make(chan error, 1)
80		go func() {
81			err := srv.Serve(ln)
82			if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, http.ErrServerClosed) {
83				errCh <- err
84				return
85			}
86			errCh <- nil
87		}()
88	
89		select {
90		case <-ctx.Done():
91			fmt.Fprintln(opts.Stderr, "\nShutting down…")
92			shutdownCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), shutdownTimeout)
93			defer cancel()
94			if err := srv.Shutdown(shutdownCtx); err != nil {
95				return fmt.Errorf("run: shutdown: %w", err)
96			}
97			return nil
98		case err := <-errCh:
99			if err != nil {
100				return fmt.Errorf("run: server error: %w", err)
101			}
102			return nil
103		}
104	}

106	// displayURL builds a browser-friendly URL. It uses the actual bound port
107	// (important when Port was 0) and rewrites wildcard bind hosts to localhost.
108	func displayURL(host string, addr net.Addr) string {
109		port := 0
110		if tcp, ok := addr.(*net.TCPAddr); ok {
111			port = tcp.Port
112		}
113		if host == "" || host == "0.0.0.0" || host == "::" {
114			host = "localhost"
115		}
116		return fmt.Sprintf("http://%s", net.JoinHostPort(host, fmt.Sprintf("%d", port)))
117	}

12	// topologyProvider fetches the declared topologies for the workspace. Each
13	// entry's Path is the on-disk system directory (the handler normalizes it to
14	// a root-relative identifier). Per-host failures are returned as messages
15	// alongside the successes so one broken host cannot hide the rest.
16	type topologyProvider func(ctx context.Context) (entries []topology.Entry, errs []string)
17	
18	// hostGraphProvider returns the default provider: it finds every scaffolded
19	// system host under root and asks each one to print its declared topology.
20	// Hosts scaffolded before the graph verb existed simply fail, which surfaces as
21	// an error the UI renders.
22	//
23	// The mechanics live in topology.RunGraph, which deploy init shares. What stays
24	// here is the dashboard's policy: never fail, report per host.
25	func hostGraphProvider(root string) topologyProvider {
26		return func(ctx context.Context) ([]topology.Entry, []string) {
27			hosts, _ := template.ListSystemHosts(root)
28			var entries []topology.Entry
29			var errs []string
30			for _, h := range hosts {
31				t, err := topology.RunGraph(ctx, h.Path)
32				if err != nil {
33					errs = append(errs, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %v", displayPath(root, h.Path), err))
34					continue
35				}
36				// The system directory is the workspace directory holding the
37				// host: components are scaffolded as its siblings.
38				entries = append(entries, topology.Entry{Path: filepath.Dir(h.Path), Topology: *t})
39			}
40			return entries, errs
41		}
42	}

44	// displayPath shortens a host directory to its root-relative form for error
45	// messages, matching the identifier space the rest of the API uses.
46	func displayPath(root, p string) string {

48			return filepath.ToSlash(rel)

37	// a missing kustomize after cloning wastes the user's time. Which ones is the
38	// caller's business — sync renders nothing, so demanding kustomize of it would
39	// be a prerequisite it never uses.

44			return nil, err
45		}

48		if err != nil {
49			return nil, err
50		}
51		resolved := cfg.Resolve(config.Flags{GitopsRepo: opts.GitopsRepo, ArgocdServer: opts.ArgocdServer})

| --- | --- |

dashboard and run a CLI command per component to get it.

# Surfacing `deploy` state in the dashboard's Integration Catalog

## Context

`intropy dashboard` is a **workspace-local, offline, read-only** view. Its package
doc is explicit (`internal/dashboard/server.go:1`): the only thing it executes is
each system host's `graph` verb. Everything else comes off local disk — scaffold
records, `AGENTS.md`/`README.md`, `local/dapr-components/*.yaml`,
`src/Process/Steps/*`, `messages/<connector>.md`.

So the catalog answers **"what did we build?"** — Template, Version, Source, Path,
Values, Pipeline steps, Dapr components, README (`DetailPanel.tsx:28-84`).

It cannot answer **"what is actually running, where, at which version, and is it
healthy?"** — even though that answer already exists as fully-structured JSON in
`intropy deploy status`. Today you leave the dashboard and run a CLI command per
component to get it.

**Outcome:** the catalog detail panel gains a deployment ladder — the environments
in promotion order with the version, digest, age, sync policy and ArgoCD
sync/health each one runs, plus the "same bits" verdict — without the dashboard
losing its zero-dependency offline startup.

Scope decisions taken: **catalog detail panel only** (no new top-level view),
**deployment ladder only** (history, sidebar badges, fleet matrix, release notes,
placeholders and derived facts are deliberately deferred — see *Deferred* at the
end).

## The data being surfaced

`internal/deploy/result.go:161` — already stable, additive-only JSON:

- `StatusResult{Component, Domain, System, Kind, Environments[], Consistent}`
- `EnvironmentStatus{Environment, AppName, OverlayPath, Onboarded, Reason,
  Release, SourceCommit, Pins[], Revision, DeployedAt, SyncPolicy, SyncStatus,
  HealthStatus, SyncedRevision, Pending}`
- `ResultPin{Image, Previous, Digest, Tag}`

`Consistent` is the headline claim the command exists to make: *promotion copies
digests rather than rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes "prod runs the bits
staging tested" a fact rather than a hope.*

Row order comes from `DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()` (`gitops/config.go:223`), a
topological sort of `promotesFrom` — **not** alphabetical. `deploy status` is
emphatic that `dev, prod, staging` tells the wrong story about a pipeline.

## Key design decision: read the cache, refresh on demand

Deploy state needs a GitOps clone — but **not** `openSession`, which locks,
fetches, and hard-resets. `gitops.CachedRoot(override)` (`repository.go:165`)
resolves the already-cached checkout with **no network, no lock, no reset**,
failing cleanly with `no cached checkout of <url> yet`. The shell completions
already rely on exactly this (`cmd/intropy/deploy.go:122`: *"Every completion here
reads the local cache only"*).

That gives a shape identical to the existing `topologyProvider`:

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| startup | unchanged — no network, no new required config |
| first `/api/deploy` request | `CachedRoot` → `ListComponents` → per-env overlay read, all local disk; cached behind a mutex like `topoMu` |
| `POST /api/deploy/refresh` | the only place paying for `gitops.Open` (lock + fetch) and the ArgoCD round trips |
| no cache / no config | a first-class *"not fetched yet"* state with the refresh affordance |

Three tiers that must degrade independently, and never into a false negative:

- **GitOps clone** → envs, versions, digests, ages, promotion order, `Consistent`
- **+ ArgoCD token** → `SyncStatus`, `HealthStatus`, `Pending`
- **absent** → renders as *unknown / not fetched*, never as *unhealthy* or *not deployed*

The codebase already encodes this distinction everywhere — `Onboarded`+`Reason`,
`StatusResult.Kind`'s doc comment, the entire reason `ChangeBasis` exists — and
the UI must not undo it.

## Implementation

### 1. `internal/gitops/repository.go` — a lock-free cached open

```go
// OpenCached returns the existing cached checkout without cloning, fetching or
// locking. Branch is empty: naming the default branch is a remote query, and a
// reader that only inspects committed files does not need it. Callers that
// write must use Open.
func OpenCached(gitopsRepoOverride string, r command.Runner) (*Repository, error)
```

Reuses `CachedRoot` (`:165`) and sets `Git: git.Client{Runner: r, Dir: dir}`.
`Close()` already tolerates a nil lock (`:139`), so the returned value is safe to
close.

### 2. `internal/deploy/status.go` — extract the pure reader

`Status()` currently welds session-open, ArgoCD observation and table rendering
together. Split out the two halves the dashboard needs, leaving `Status()` as the
thin composition so **CLI behaviour is unchanged**:

```go
// StatusOf reads one component's deployment state from an already-open
// repository. Git only: it renders nothing, touches no network, and never fails
// on a single unreadable environment.
func StatusOf(ctx context.Context, repo *gitops.Repository, deployCfg *gitops.DeployConfig,
    coord gitops.Coordinate, comp *gitops.ComponentConfig) StatusResult

// ObserveArgo fills SyncStatus, HealthStatus, SyncedRevision and Pending in
// place. Unreachable ArgoCD is a warning on Stderr, never a failure.
func ObserveArgo(ctx context.Context, repo *gitops.Repository,
    deployCfg *gitops.DeployConfig, opts ArgoOptions, rows []EnvironmentStatus)

type ArgoOptions struct {
    Server         string    // --argocd-server, wins over everything
    FallbackServer string    // argocdServer from user config
    UserAgent      string
    Stderr         io.Writer
}
```

`StatusOf` is `statusEnvironments` + `readOverlayState` + `SyncPolicy` +
`consistent` — all of which exist already (`:77`, `:106`, `:222`). `ObserveArgo`
is today's `observeArgo` (`:157`) with `*session` replaced by `ArgoOptions`, so it
no longer depends on package-private state.

### 3. `internal/dashboard/deploy.go` (new) — the provider

Mirrors `topology.go` exactly: a func-typed seam so tests stub it, best-effort,
reports per component.

```go
// deployProvider reads deployment state for the workspace. refresh pays for a
// locked fetch and the ArgoCD round trips; otherwise it reads the cache.
type deployProvider func(ctx context.Context, refresh bool) deployReport

// deployReport is the /api/deploy payload.
type deployReport struct {
    // Configured reports that a GitOps repository is configured at all;
    // Fetched that a checkout was found and read. Reason explains a false.
    // These three exist so "nobody asked" can never render as "not deployed".
    Configured bool   `json:"configured"`
    Fetched    bool   `json:"fetched"`
    Reason     string `json:"reason,omitempty"`

    Repo string `json:"repo,omitempty"`

    // ArgocdRead reports whether sync and health were actually read. False
    // leaves those fields empty on every row and means unknown, not unhealthy.
    ArgocdRead bool `json:"argocdRead"`

    // Environments is deploy.yaml's environments in promotion order, with each
    // one's sync policy — the ladder's rungs, independent of any component.
    Environments []deployEnvironment `json:"environments,omitempty"`

    // Components is keyed by the root-relative workspace path the catalog uses,
    // so the frontend joins by the identifier it already has. A component with
    // no unambiguous workspace match is absent here and named in Unmatched.
    Components map[string]deploy.StatusResult `json:"components"`

    // Unmatched names GitOps components no workspace integration claims, and
    // Ambiguous those whose name resolves to more than one. Both are reported
    // rather than guessed around.
    Unmatched []string `json:"unmatched,omitempty"`
    Ambiguous []string `json:"ambiguous,omitempty"`

    Errors []string `json:"errors,omitempty"`
}

type deployEnvironment struct {
    Name         string   `json:"name"`
    Sync         string   `json:"sync"`
    PromotesFrom []string `json:"promotesFrom,omitempty"`
}
```

Embedding `deploy.StatusResult` verbatim means the dashboard JSON matches
`intropy deploy status -o json` field for field — one contract to learn.

**The join.** Catalog entries are keyed by root-relative workspace path; GitOps by
`Coordinate{Domain, System, Component}`. Match a `Coordinate` against each
`integrationSummary`'s `{Domain, System, Name}` (`handlers.go:68`), case-folded to
match `sys create`'s kebab-casing. Exactly one match wins; zero → `Unmatched`; more
than one → `Ambiguous` and **no** status is served for it. Per memory, component
names collide across customers and `config.yaml` is a single flat `gitopsRepo`, so
ambiguity is real, not theoretical — `gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` already

2. **Sidebar status dots** — makes the catalog scannable; needs the ladder's data

3. **Fleet matrix view** — component × environment. Genuinely new capability

# Surfacing deployment state in the dashboard's Integration Catalog

## Context

`intropy dashboard` is a **workspace-local, offline, read-only** view. Its package
doc is explicit (`internal/dashboard/server.go:1`): the only thing it executes is
each system host's `graph` verb. Everything else comes off local disk — scaffold
records, `AGENTS.md`/`README.md`, `local/dapr-components/*.yaml`,
`src/Process/Steps/*`, `messages/<connector>.md`.

So the catalog answers **"what did we build?"** — Template, Version, Source, Path,
Values, Pipeline steps, Dapr components, README (`DetailPanel.tsx:28-84`).

It cannot answer **"what is running, where, at which version, and is it healthy?"**
even though that answer already exists as stable, structured JSON in
`intropy deploy status`. Today you leave the dashboard and run a CLI command per
component.

**Outcome:** the catalog detail panel gains a deployment ladder — every environment
in promotion order with the release, digests, age, sync policy and (after an
explicit refresh) ArgoCD sync/health, plus the "same bits" verdict — while the
dashboard keeps its zero-dependency offline startup and never interferes with a
running `intropy deploy`.

**Scope taken:** catalog detail panel only (no new top-level view); deployment
ladder only. Release manifests, deploy history, sidebar chips and the fleet matrix
are analysed and deferred at the end.

## The data being surfaced

`internal/deploy/result.go:161`, already stable and additive-only:

- `StatusResult{Component, Domain, System, Kind, Environments[], Consistent}`
- `EnvironmentStatus{Environment, AppName, OverlayPath, Onboarded, Reason,
  Release, SourceCommit, Pins[], Revision, DeployedAt, SyncPolicy, SyncStatus,
  HealthStatus, SyncedRevision, Pending}`
- `ResultPin{Image, Previous, Digest, Tag}`

`Consistent` is the claim the command exists to make: *promotion copies digests
rather than rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes "prod runs the bits staging
tested" a fact rather than a hope.*

Row order comes from `DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()` (`gitops/config.go:223`), a
topological sort of `promotesFrom`. **Not alphabetical** — `deploy status` is
emphatic that `dev, prod, staging` tells the wrong story about a pipeline.

Note what is free: `EnvironmentStatus.Release` is read from the overlay's
`deploy.internal/release` annotation (`status.go:128`), so **the version each
environment runs needs no registry access at all.** Only release *notes* do.

## Key decision: pure GET off the cache, network only on an explicit refresh

Deploy state needs a GitOps checkout — but **not** `openSession`, which locks,
fetches and hard-resets. `gitops.CachedRoot(override)` (`repository.go:165`)
resolves the existing checkout with no network, no lock and no reset, failing
cleanly with `no cached checkout of <url> yet`. Four commands already depend on it
for exactly this reason (`cmd/intropy/deploy.go:122`: *"Every completion here reads
the local cache only"*).

**The decisive argument is not latency, it is the lock.** `acquireLock`
(`repository.go:194`) is `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` and on contention returns *"another
intropy deploy is already using the cached GitOps checkout"*. A dashboard that
fetched on page load would intermittently either break a concurrent
`intropy deploy` or fail with that message in a background browser tab. Neither is
acceptable in a long-lived viewer.

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| startup | unchanged — no network, no lock, no new required config |
| `GET /api/deploy` | `CachedRoot` → `ListComponents` → per-env overlay reads. Local disk only. Cached behind a mutex, exactly like `topoMu` |
| `POST /api/deploy/refresh` | the **only** place that fetches (`gitops.Open`) and the only place that talks to ArgoCD |
| no config / no checkout | a first-class named state, not an empty ladder |

Consequence to accept, not paper over: a lockless read can see a tree mid
`ResetHard`+`Clean` from a concurrent deploy. Every file read here already degrades
to `Onboarded:false` + `Reason` rather than failing, so a torn read shows as one
bad row that the next refresh corrects, and the report carries the HEAD sha it
read. Do **not** add `LOCK_SH` to `acquireLock` — that changes `deploy`'s
exclusivity guarantee to buy a caveat the never-fails contract already absorbs.

### The honesty contract

A bool cannot distinguish "not configured" from "not onboarded", and that
distinction is the whole point. Four named states:

| state | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unconfigured` | no `gitopsRepo` by flag, env or file |
| `no-checkout` | configured, but never cloned on this machine |
| `unreadable` | cloned, but no usable `deploy.yaml` |
| `ready` | surveyed |

Only when `ready` does an unmatched integration say anything *about the
integration*. The other three are statements about the dashboard and must never be
phrased as if they were about the integration. This mirrors what the Go types
already encode — `Onboarded`+`Reason`, `StatusResult.Kind`'s doc comment, and the
entire reason `ChangeBasis` exists.

## Implementation

### 1. `internal/deploy/status.go` — decouple the reader from the session

`readOverlayState` (`:106`) takes `repo *gitops.Repository` but only ever uses
`repo.Root` (via `gitops.ResolveOverlay`) and `repo.Git` (via `LastCommitAt`).
Nothing it does needs a lock:

```go
func readOverlayState(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client,
    coord gitops.Coordinate, comp *gitops.ComponentConfig, env string) EnvironmentStatus
```

`g == nil` skips the `Revision`/`DeployedAt` read — both are already documented as
"empty when the path has no history", so nil is an existing honest shape, not a new
one. In-package callers become `readOverlayState(ctx, repo.Root, &repo.Git, …)`.

### 2. `internal/deploy/status.go` — extract the per-component read

```go
// ComponentStatus reads one component's state in every environment it declares,
// from a checkout already on disk. Status without the session, the ArgoCD call
// or the report: no lock, no network, no output. Nothing here fails — an
// unreadable environment comes back Onboarded false with a Reason.
func ComponentStatus(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client,
    deployCfg *gitops.DeployConfig, coord gitops.Coordinate,
    comp *gitops.ComponentConfig) StatusResult
```

Body is `:52-60` plus the `StatusResult` assembly from `reportStatus` (`:244-251`).
`Status()` becomes session → `locateComponent` → `ComponentStatus` →
`observeArgo` → `reportStatus`. `statusEnvironments` (`:77`), `readOverlayState`,
`consistent` (`:222`) and `pinSignature` (`:202`) are all reused, none duplicated.

**The refactor is done when every existing test in `internal/deploy` passes
unedited.** That is the "CLI behaves identically" assertion — do not weaken it.

### 3. Serve the prose; do not re-derive it in TypeScript

`summarise` (`:352`) and `notes` (`:435`) are the honesty layer of this whole
feature — the sentences that separate *"these two run different bits"* from
*"there is nothing to compare here"*, and that explain an empty digest for a
`kind: shared` component. The Go tests assert on that prose. Reimplementing it in
React is the single most likely way this feature becomes dishonest, because two
implementations means two conclusions from one set of rows and only one of them is
tested.

Two additive fields, which `StatusResult`'s own doc licenses ("field names are
stable and additive-only"):

```go
// Summary and Notes are the sentences the plain table prints beneath itself:
// what the environments collectively run, and the qualifications — what could
// not be read, what pins a tag, what is waiting. They travel in the result so a
// second presenter cannot draw a different conclusion from the same rows.
Summary string   `json:"summary"`
Notes   []string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
```

`ComponentStatus` fills them via the existing functions; `reportStatus` reads them
back off the result so there is one call site. **This additively changes
`deploy status -o json`** — it gains prose the plain output already showed. That is
an improvement, and it is the recommendation; the alternative (a dashboard-local
wrapper struct) means two structs asserting the same claim.

### 4. `internal/deploy/survey.go` (new) — every component, one pass, no lock

```go
type SurveyOptions struct {
    // Root is a checkout already on disk. Survey never clones, fetches or
    // locks: the caller either owns a session or, like the dashboard, is
    // reading what an earlier command left behind.
    Root string

    // Git reads each overlay's last-changed commit, which is what dates a
    // deployment. Nil skips it.
    Git *git.Client

    // Coords narrows the survey. Empty means every component in the tree.
    Coords []gitops.Coordinate
}

// SurveyEntry is one component's state, or the reason it has none.
type SurveyEntry struct {
    Coordinate gitops.Coordinate
    Status     *StatusResult

    // Error is why this component could not be described — an unreadable or
    // invalid component.yaml. Status is then nil. One malformed component never
    // costs the caller the rest of the tree.
    Error string
}

// Survey reads every component's state from one checkout. N calls to Status
// would take the exclusive lock N times, fetch N times, and could only hand
// back rendered text.
func Survey(ctx context.Context, opts SurveyOptions) (*gitops.DeployConfig, []SurveyEntry, []string)
```

Implementation: `gitops.ListComponents(root)` — one glob, `layout.go:142` — →
`LoadComponentConfig` → `ComponentStatus`, in the order `ListComponents` returns.

Cost with `Git` set is one `git log -1 -- <path>` per component per environment:
roughly a second for 30 components × 3 envs on a warm repo. Acceptable behind the
lazy cache, which today already fronts a `dotnet build`. If measurement later
demands it, a single `git log --name-only --format` pass over `domains/` replaces
the loop.

### 5. `internal/dashboard/deploy.go` (new) — provider and join

Mirrors `topology.go`, for the reason it already states (`:23`): *"The mechanics
live in topology.RunGraph… What stays here is the dashboard's policy."* `gitops`
and `deploy` stay ignorant of the workspace identifier space.

```go
// deployProvider surveys the GitOps repository. Like topologyProvider it never
// fails: an unconfigured repository, an absent checkout or an unreadable one
// each come back as a Source state, because "we do not know" and "it is not
// deployed" must never render the same.
type deployProvider func(ctx context.Context, opts refreshOptions) deploySurvey

// refreshOptions is what a refresh is allowed to do beyond re-reading the
// cache. The zero value is a pure local read, which is what a GET always gets.
type refreshOptions struct {
    Fetch  bool // take the lock and fetch from the remote
    Argocd bool // read sync and health
}
```

**The join.** The codebase states the rule twice — `init.go:493` (*"the source
workspace's own layout, which every customer integrations tree mirrors from the
deployment tree"*) and `initmodel.go:134` `matchScaffolds` (*"a component's
directory basename, and its scaffold record's `values.appId`. Both are matched —
directory first"*). Follow the established convention rather than invent one. First
hit wins:

| # | `matchedBy` | rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `coordinate` | `{Domain, System, Name}` == `{c.Domain, c.System, c.Component}`, exactly one hit |
| 2 | `system` | integration has no domain: `{System, Name}` matches, exactly one hit |
| 3 | `appId` | `values.appId == c.Component` **and** `System == c.System`, exactly one hit |

Case-folded, to match `sys create`'s kebab-casing.

**There is deliberately no bare-name rule.** Per memory, component names collide
across customers and `config.yaml` is a single flat `gitopsRepo`;
`gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` (`layout.go:53`) exists precisely because a name
occurs in several places. Matching on name alone would attribute another system's
production digest to this integration — the worst failure available here, and it
must be structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

Outcomes: one hit → `matched:true` + `matchedBy` + `status`; no hit → `matched:false`
with a reason naming same-named components at other coordinates as `candidates`, so
a mislaid domain reads as a mislaid domain; more than one hit → `matched:false`,
both `candidates`, and **`status: nil`** — never resolved by picking one. GitOps
components no integration claims go in `orphans`, because a deployed workload
nobody accounts for is a finding, not noise.

### 6. `internal/dashboard/handlers.go` — wire it

`newHandler`'s parameter list is about to grow, so collapse it once:

```go
type providers struct {
    topology topologyProvider
    deploy   deployProvider
}

func newHandler(root, version string, p providers) (http.Handler, error)
```

Cache state on `apiServer` mirrors `topoMu/topoLoaded/topoEntries/topoErrs`
(`:32-35`) field for field; the accessor mirrors `cachedTopologies` (`:258-271`).
Two routes beside the topology pair (`:99-100`):

```go
mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/deploy", api.deployState)          // always refreshOptions{}
mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/deploy/refresh", api.refreshDeploy) // Fetch+Argocd
```

Payload:

```go
type deployReport struct {
    // Source says where this came from and how current it is. Always present,
    // including when nothing could be read — it is what keeps "no GitOps
    // repository is configured" from rendering as "not deployed".
    Source deploySource `json:"source"`

    // Integrations covers every catalogued integration, keyed by the same
    // root-relative path /api/integrations uses. Always an array; an unmatched
    // integration is present and says why.
    Integrations []integrationDeploy `json:"integrations"`

    // Orphans are GitOps components no workspace integration claims.
    Orphans []deploy.StatusResult `json:"orphans,omitempty"`

    Errors []string `json:"errors,omitempty"`
}

type deploySource struct {
    State string `json:"state"` // unconfigured | no-checkout | unreadable | ready

    // Reason is the CLI's own message, verbatim: RequireGitopsRepo's list of
    // every way to supply the URL, or LoadDeployConfig's complaint. Served
    // rather than restated, so the dashboard cannot tell a user something the
    // command line would not.
    Reason string `json:"reason,omitempty"`
    Repo   string `json:"repo,omitempty"`

    // Revision is the checkout's HEAD — exactly what was read. Fetched false
    // means this is whatever the last deploy command left on disk. ArgocdRead
    // false leaves sync and health empty on every row, and means unknown.
    Revision   string    `json:"revision,omitempty"`
    ReadAt     time.Time `json:"readAt"`
    Fetched    bool      `json:"fetched"`
    ArgocdRead bool      `json:"argocdRead"`

    // Environments is deploy.yaml's environments in promotion order, so a
    // component onboarded to a subset can be laid out against the full set.
    Environments []string `json:"environments,omitempty"`
}

type integrationDeploy struct {
    Path        string   `json:"path"`
    Matched     bool     `json:"matched"`
    MatchedBy   string   `json:"matchedBy,omitempty"`
    MatchReason string   `json:"matchReason,omitempty"`
    Candidates  []string `json:"candidates,omitempty"`

    Status *deploy.StatusResult `json:"status,omitempty"`
}
```

Embedding `deploy.StatusResult` verbatim means the dashboard payload matches
`deploy status -o json` field for field — one contract to learn.

**Deliberately not on `GET /api/integrations/{path}`**: that endpoint must stay
instant and offline-pure, and N detail requests would each need the same survey.
One report, indexed by path on the client — the shape `FlowView` already uses.

ArgoCD reads come from today's `observeArgo` (`:157`), extracted to take an
`io.Writer` for warnings that the handler collects into `errors[]` instead of the
server's stderr. Its `ErrUnreachable` early return (stop asking after the first
failure) is exactly right for a dashboard — preserve it verbatim.

### 7. Frontend

`web/src/api.ts` — mirror the Go structs 1:1, which is the file's stated job
(`:1-3`): `ResultPin`, `EnvironmentStatus`, `StatusResult` (including `summary`
and `notes`), `DeploySource`, `IntegrationDeploy`, `DeployReport`. Then two lines
on the `api` object beside `topologies`/`refreshTopologies` (`:253-256`):

```ts
deploy: () => getJSON<DeployReport>('/api/deploy'),
refreshDeploy: () => requestJSON<DeployReport>('/api/deploy/refresh', { method: 'POST' }),
```

`web/src/App.tsx` — one `useState<DeployReport | null>`, fetched in the existing
mount effect beside `listIntegrations()` (`:77-86`); a `Map<string,
IntegrationDeploy>` via `useMemo`; passed into `DetailPanel`. It is workspace-wide
data, so it must **not** go in the per-selection effect at `:95-105`. No new `View`.

`web/src/components/DetailPanel.tsx` — a new `<Section title="Deployment">` placed
**directly under the meta-grid, above Values**: where an integration runs is more
operationally interesting than its scaffold values. Uses the exported
`Section`/`Meta` primitives (`:88-115`) that `FlowDetail.tsx` already reuses.

1. **Verdict** — `status.summary`, rendered as served, with a state marker from
   `consistent`.
2. **Table**, one row per environment in served order (last row = furthest
   downstream, matching the CLI):

   | Environment | Release | Image / digest | Age | Sync | Health |
   | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

   - *Environment* — name, plus a `manual` chip when `syncPolicy === 'manual'` and
     a `waiting` chip when `pending`. An unspent manual gate is a resting state,
     **not** a fault, and must read that way.
   - *Release* — `release`, else `@` + 7-char `sourceCommit`, else `—`. Same rule as
     `releaseCell` (`:283`); the `@` prefix is what stops a commit reading as a
     version.
   - *Image / digest* — **all** pins, one line each, full digest in `title`. This is
     the one place to improve on the CLI: `digestCell` (`:300`) shows only `pins[0]`
     because *"one row per environment is what makes the table scannable"* and a
     note has to cover the rest. A web panel has the room. A tag pin renders `:tag`
     in a warning tone.
   - *Age* — from `deployedAt`, truncated to one unit exactly as `humanAge` (`:333`)
     does: 119 minutes is `1h`, never `2h`, because *"a deployment reading as older
     than it is would be read as a change someone else already reviewed."*
   - *Sync / Health* — as served. When `source.argocdRead` is false, collapse both
     columns and print one line: *"ArgoCD was not read, so sync and health are
     unknown — this says nothing about what the overlays pin."* An empty column
     would read as unhealthy.
   - `onboarded: false` — render the row, muted, with `reason` spanning the data
     cells. Never omit it: `statusEnvironments` (`:77`) deliberately includes an
     environment the component declares that `deploy.yaml` does not define, and that
     is the fact an operator most needs.
3. **Notes** — `status.notes` as a muted list.
4. **The four unknown states** — no spinner, no empty table. `unconfigured` shows
   `source.reason` verbatim (already `RequireGitopsRepo`'s full list of ways to
   supply the URL); `no-checkout` says the repo is configured but not cloned here
   and to run any deploy command once; `unreadable` shows `LoadDeployConfig`'s
   message; `ready` + `!matched` shows `matchReason` with `candidates`.
5. **Provenance footer** when `ready`: *"read from {repo} at {short sha}, {age}
   ago"*, and when `!fetched`, *"not fetched from the remote — this is the checkout
   your last deploy command left behind."* Beside it a **Refresh** button
   mirroring `.flow-refresh` (`FlowView.tsx:261`) — same class family, disabled
   while pending. Lock contention arrives as an `errors[]` entry, never a 500.

### 8. Docs

- `internal/dashboard/server.go:1` — the invariant must be **restated, not quietly
  broken**: the only things executed are each host's `graph` verb and read-only
  reads of the cached GitOps checkout, and the only network access is an explicit
  refresh.
- `README.md` — the dashboard is absent from the command overview (`:162-195`)
  entirely; add it, and a paragraph in the deploy section on what the catalog now
  shows and that a GET shows the *cached* checkout.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md:256` layout table — add `internal/dashboard/deploy.go` and
  `internal/deploy/survey.go`.

## Tests

House style: `t.Chdir(tmp)` + `writeScaffold` + a `testHandlerWith*` helper +
literal-key assertions on `map[string]any`, table-driven where cases are parallel
(`internal/dashboard/dashboard_test.go:41-69`, `internal/deploy/status_test.go`).

`internal/deploy/survey_test.go` (new), over `gitopstest.NewRepo` fixtures:

- **`TestSurveyDoesNotTakeTheCheckoutLock`** — hold an exclusive flock on
  `CheckoutDir(...)+".lock"`, assert Survey still succeeds. **This pins the entire
  offline design; write it first.**
- reads every component from one checkout, rows in promotion order, `Consistent` right
- an invalid `component.yaml` sets that entry's `Error` and leaves siblings intact
- `Coords` narrows the tree; `Git: nil` leaves `Revision`/`DeployedAt` empty without panicking

`internal/deploy/status_test.go` (extend): `Summary` is byte-identical to the
sentence the plain output prints and `Notes` to the lines under it — the anti-drift
test. Every other existing test passes **unedited**.

`internal/dashboard/deploy_test.go` (new), with `emptyDeploy`/`testHandlerWithDeploy`
beside the existing `emptyTopo`/`testHandlerWithTopo`:

- `unconfigured` — reason names `INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO` and the config path;
  `integrations` is `[]` not `null`; every integration present with
  `matched:false`; **no reason string contains "not deployed"**
- `no-checkout` names the repository and reads differently from `unconfigured`
- one test per join tier (`coordinate`, `system`, `appId`)
- ambiguity → `matched:false`, both `candidates`, `status == nil`
- **never matches on bare component name** when the workspace domain disagrees
- orphans reported; one broken component becomes an `errors[]` entry without hiding the rest
- GET is cached until refresh — same shape as `TestTopologyCachedUntilRefresh`
- **GET never fetches and never touches ArgoCD**: assert the provider received the
  zero `refreshOptions`

Frontend has no test runner (`web/package.json` is `tsc -b` only), so the Go
handler tests are the only guard on the JSON contract — assert literal key names.
Run `cd web && npm run typecheck` as part of the change.

## Verification

```sh
make                       # build + go test ./...
go test ./internal/deploy/... ./internal/dashboard/...
cd web && npm run typecheck
```

Then the four states in order, which *are* the feature:

1. **Unconfigured** — `env -u INTROPY_GITOPS_REPO ./intropy dashboard ./examples`
   with no `gitopsRepo` in config. The catalog must look exactly as it does today
   plus one explanatory line. `curl -s localhost:8730/api/deploy | jq .source`
   shows `state: "unconfigured"`.
2. **No checkout** — set `gitopsRepo`, move `~/Library/Caches/intropy/gitops`
   aside. Expect `no-checkout` naming the repo, and the Refresh affordance.
3. **Ready, cache only** — run `intropy deploy status <component>` once to warm the
   cache, then reload. Ladder populates with versions, digests and ages;
   `fetched: false` and `argocdRead: false`; Sync/Health collapsed to the
   explanatory line, nothing reported unhealthy.
4. **Refreshed** — click Refresh with `ARGOCD_AUTH_TOKEN` set. `fetched: true`,
   `argocdRead: true`, sync/health populated.

Then prove the GET is inert and the lock is respected:

```sh
# with a deploy holding the lock, a GET must still answer
./intropy deploy order-extractor --env dev &   # holds LOCK_EX
curl -s localhost:8730/api/deploy | jq .source.state    # => "ready"
```

Cross-check one real component against the CLI — they read the same structs, so
they must agree exactly:

```sh
./intropy deploy status order-extractor -o json | jq '{summary, consistent}'
curl -s localhost:8730/api/deploy \
  | jq '.integrations[] | select(.path=="sales/ordersync/order-extract") | .status | {summary, consistent}'
```

UI dev loop: `make web-dev` (proxies `/api` → `127.0.0.1:8730`). Per
`CONTRIBUTING.md:76-78`, run `make web-clean` before committing so a locally-built
`web/dist/index.html` does not land in the diff.

## Deferred (analysed, not in this phase)

Ranked by value; all rest on the same provider and `Survey`.

1. **Deployment history timeline.** `publish.go:19` writes
   `Deploy-Component/Domain/System/Env/Release/Promoted-From/Image/Digest/Source-Commit/By/Cli`
   trailers, and the doc comment says *"they are a format, not just a message:
   `deploy history` reads them back"* — **but `deploy history` does not exist.** The
   readers do: `git.Client.Log` (`git/client.go:311`) and `Trailers` (`:413`,
   already used at `diff.go:211`). `Log("HEAD", coord.OverlayRelPath(env))` +
   `Trailers` per commit is a complete per-environment audit trail — who deployed
   what version, from which commit, deploy vs promotion — offline, no ArgoCD, no
   registry. Best built as the promised CLI command with the dashboard as a second
   consumer. **The largest piece of latent value in these two commands.**
2. **Sidebar chip.** Not a health dot — the sidebar has no room to be honest, and a
   red dot beside "not configured" is exactly the lie this design exists to avoid.
   Instead: when `ready && matched`, a right-aligned chip with the release the
   **last** environment in promotion order runs (usually prod) — the most-asked
   question — reusing `.count`/`.chip-sub`. A `!` marker when `consistent === false`,
   which is a positive finding and safe to render. **Anything else renders nothing
   at all**; no chip is no claim, and that rule is load-bearing.
3. **Fleet matrix view** — component × environment. Genuinely new capability
   (`deploy status` is one component at a time) at the same survey cost.
4. **Release history** — `release.ListVersions` (`artifact.go:126`) + `Pull` give
   notes, `Changes[]`, digests and `ChangeBasis.Describe()` (serve that string, for
   the same reason `summary` is served). Registry auth, so: explicit click only,
   never in the report. `ErrNotFound` on the releases repo means *never released*,
   not a failure.
5. **Onboarding gaps** — outstanding `REPLACE-ME-*` placeholders per component
   (`placeholder.go`, `scanPlaceholders` currently unexported).
6. **Derived facts in the meta grid** — workload kind (`initmodel.go:235`
   `workloadFor`: extractor ⇒ CronJob), Dapr app-id, declared images, `sourcePaths`,
   ArgoCD app name (`Coordinate.AppName(env)` = `domain-system-component-env`),
   namespace.
7. **Integration drawer in the flow view** — `FlowDetail.tsx`'s `FlowSelection`
   union covers only `topic` and `connector`; widening it with
   `{kind:'integration'; path}` would put the ladder on the canvas.

## Explicitly not recommended

- **Surfacing `deploy diff` output.** `DiffResult.Diff` is a fully rendered
  Kubernetes manifest diff at two revisions, including everything under
  `base/secrets/`. It is the one command whose JSON carries cluster resource
  *content* rather than references — wrong for a browser tab, its history, or a
  screenshot. Link out to the CLI.
- **Writes from the dashboard** (deploy / promote / sync). The read-only promise in
  the package doc is load-bearing and the production gate is deliberately
  CLI-and-review-shaped.
- **Fetching on page load, background polling, or `--watch`.** `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`
  means a background tab would intermittently break the user's deploy, and it turns
  a viewer into an unattended agent holding a cluster token.
- **Calling `deploy.Status()` per component.** N exclusive locks, N fetches, and it
  can only return rendered text.
- **Re-deriving `summarise`, `notes`, `releaseCell`, `digestCell` or
  `ChangeBasis.Describe()` in TypeScript.** These are the honesty layer; two
  implementations means two conclusions and only one is tested.
- **Any bare-component-name fallback in the join.**
- **A boolean `deployAvailable` instead of the four states.**
- **Inferring deployment from directory shape.** The codebase never guesses
  (`FlowView.tsx:219` renders an empty state rather than a guessed graph).

## Sharp edges found while reading

- `Manifest.Source.Repo` is the **GitOps** repo URL, not the source repo
  (`release/create.go:137`). Do not label it "source repository" in a later phase.
- Releases are addressed off `ReleasesRepo(comp.Images[0].Name)` (`view.go:62`) — a
  multi-image component has **one** release stream; the UI must not imply otherwise.
- `EnvironmentConfig.Scratch` is parsed but never acted on (`config.go:125`). Don't
  build UI meaning onto it.
- `Deploy-By`/`CreatedBy` carry operator emails scraped from
  `GITLAB_USER_EMAIL`/`GITHUB_ACTOR`/`USER` (`publish.go:232`, `create.go:292`).
  Fine for a server bound to `127.0.0.1` by default; worth remembering if `--addr`
  is ever opened up.

## The gap

The dashboard is strictly design-time. Every byte it serves comes off the local workspace — scaffold records, host `graph` verb, Dapr YAML, README. So the catalog answers *"what did we build?"* and cannot answer *"what's running, where, at which version, is it healthy?"* — even though `deploy status` already produces exactly that as stable JSON (`internal/deploy/result.go:161`).

## Highest-value findings

**1. `deploy status` is a ready-made ladder.** `StatusResult` + `EnvironmentStatus` carry release version, per-image digests, deploy age, sync policy, ArgoCD sync/health, `Pending` (unspent manual gate), and `Consistent` — the "prod runs the bits staging tested" claim. Row order comes from `PromotionOrder()`, a topological sort of `promotesFrom`, not alphabetical.

**2. `deploy history` is promised in code but doesn't exist.** `publish.go:18` says the commit trailers *"are a format, not just a message: `deploy history` reads them back"* — and nothing reads them back. Both readers already exist (`git.Log`, `git.Trailers`). `Log("HEAD", overlayPath)` + trailers per commit = a complete per-environment audit trail (who deployed what version, from which commit, deploy vs promotion), fully offline. **This is the biggest piece of latent value in the two commands** — I put it first in the deferred list rather than phase 1 since you scoped to the ladder.

**3. The offline invariant survives, and the reason isn't latency.** `gitops.CachedRoot` reads the existing checkout with no network, no lock, no reset — four commands already rely on it for shell completion. The decisive argument against fetching on page load is that `acquireLock` is `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`: a background browser tab would intermittently break a concurrent `intropy deploy`. So GETs read the cache; only an explicit Refresh fetches or touches ArgoCD.

**4. The honesty problem is the actual design work.** "GitOps not configured", "never cloned here", "not onboarded to this env", and "not deployed" are four different statements, and three of them are about the dashboard rather than the integration. Hence a four-state `source.state` rather than a bool, and no bare-component-name join fallback — names collide across customers, and a wrong match would attribute another system's production digest to your integration.

**5. Serve the prose, don't port it.** `summarise` and `notes` (`status.go:352`, `:435`) are the honesty layer, and the Go tests assert on them. Re-implementing in TypeScript would silently drift, so I add `Summary`/`Notes` to `StatusResult` — additive, and it also fixes `deploy status -o json` currently omitting prose the plain output shows.

**6. One place the web should beat the CLI:** `digestCell` shows only `pins[0]` because a terminal row has no space. A panel does, so show every image.

Two things I recommend against: surfacing `deploy diff` (its JSON embeds rendered manifests including `base/secrets/`), and any write path from the dashboard.

# Surfacing deployment state in the dashboard's Integration Catalog

## Context

`intropy dashboard` is a **workspace-local, offline, read-only** view. Its package
doc is explicit (`internal/dashboard/server.go:1`): the only thing it executes is
each system host's `graph` verb. Everything else comes off local disk — scaffold
records, `AGENTS.md`/`README.md`, `local/dapr-components/*.yaml`,
`src/Process/Steps/*`, `messages/<connector>.md`.

So the catalog answers **"what did we build?"** — Template, Version, Source, Path,
Values, Pipeline steps, Dapr components, README (`DetailPanel.tsx:28-84`).

It cannot answer **"what is running, where, at which version, and is it healthy?"**
even though that answer already exists as stable, structured JSON in
`intropy deploy status`. Today you leave the dashboard and run a CLI command per
component.

**Outcome:** the catalog detail panel gains a deployment ladder — every environment
in promotion order with the release, digests, age, sync policy and (after an
explicit refresh) ArgoCD sync/health, plus the "same bits" verdict — while the
dashboard keeps its zero-dependency offline startup and never interferes with a
running `intropy deploy`.

**Scope taken:** catalog detail panel only (no new top-level view); deployment
ladder only. Release manifests, deploy history, sidebar chips and the fleet matrix
are analysed and deferred at the end.

## The data being surfaced

`internal/deploy/result.go:161`, already stable and additive-only:

- `StatusResult{Component, Domain, System, Kind, Environments[], Consistent}`
- `EnvironmentStatus{Environment, AppName, OverlayPath, Onboarded, Reason,
  Release, SourceCommit, Pins[], Revision, DeployedAt, SyncPolicy, SyncStatus,
  HealthStatus, SyncedRevision, Pending}`
- `ResultPin{Image, Previous, Digest, Tag}`

`Consistent` is the claim the command exists to make: *promotion copies digests
rather than rebuilding, so agreement here is what makes "prod runs the bits staging
tested" a fact rather than a hope.*

Row order comes from `DeployConfig.PromotionOrder()` (`gitops/config.go:223`), a
topological sort of `promotesFrom`. **Not alphabetical** — `deploy status` is
emphatic that `dev, prod, staging` tells the wrong story about a pipeline.

Note what is free: `EnvironmentStatus.Release` is read from the overlay's
`deploy.internal/release` annotation (`status.go:128`), so **the version each
environment runs needs no registry access at all.** Only release *notes* do.

## Key decision: pure GET off the cache, network only on an explicit refresh

Deploy state needs a GitOps checkout — but **not** `openSession`, which locks,
fetches and hard-resets. `gitops.CachedRoot(override)` (`repository.go:165`)
resolves the existing checkout with no network, no lock and no reset, failing
cleanly with `no cached checkout of <url> yet`. Four commands already depend on it
for exactly this reason (`cmd/intropy/deploy.go:122`: *"Every completion here reads
the local cache only"*).

**The decisive argument is not latency, it is the lock.** `acquireLock`
(`repository.go:194`) is `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` and on contention returns *"another
intropy deploy is already using the cached GitOps checkout"*. A dashboard that
fetched on page load would intermittently either break a concurrent
`intropy deploy` or fail with that message in a background browser tab. Neither is
acceptable in a long-lived viewer.

| When | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| startup | unchanged — no network, no lock, no new required config |
| `GET /api/deploy` | `CachedRoot` → `ListComponents` → per-env overlay reads. Local disk only. Cached behind a mutex, exactly like `topoMu` |
| `POST /api/deploy/refresh` | the **only** place that fetches (`gitops.Open`) and the only place that talks to ArgoCD |
| no config / no checkout | a first-class named state, not an empty ladder |

Consequence to accept, not paper over: a lockless read can see a tree mid
`ResetHard`+`Clean` from a concurrent deploy. Every file read here already degrades
to `Onboarded:false` + `Reason` rather than failing, so a torn read shows as one
bad row that the next refresh corrects, and the report carries the HEAD sha it
read. Do **not** add `LOCK_SH` to `acquireLock` — that changes `deploy`'s
exclusivity guarantee to buy a caveat the never-fails contract already absorbs.

### The honesty contract

A bool cannot distinguish "not configured" from "not onboarded", and that
distinction is the whole point. Four named states:

| state | meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `unconfigured` | no `gitopsRepo` by flag, env or file |
| `no-checkout` | configured, but never cloned on this machine |
| `unreadable` | cloned, but no usable `deploy.yaml` |
| `ready` | surveyed |

Only when `ready` does an unmatched integration say anything *about the
integration*. The other three are statements about the dashboard and must never be
phrased as if they were about the integration. This mirrors what the Go types
already encode — `Onboarded`+`Reason`, `StatusResult.Kind`'s doc comment, and the
entire reason `ChangeBasis` exists.

## Implementation

### 1. `internal/deploy/status.go` — decouple the reader from the session

`readOverlayState` (`:106`) takes `repo *gitops.Repository` but only ever uses
`repo.Root` (via `gitops.ResolveOverlay`) and `repo.Git` (via `LastCommitAt`).
Nothing it does needs a lock:

```go
func readOverlayState(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client,
    coord gitops.Coordinate, comp *gitops.ComponentConfig, env string) EnvironmentStatus
```

`g == nil` skips the `Revision`/`DeployedAt` read — both are already documented as
"empty when the path has no history", so nil is an existing honest shape, not a new
one. In-package callers become `readOverlayState(ctx, repo.Root, &repo.Git, …)`.

### 2. `internal/deploy/status.go` — extract the per-component read

```go
// ComponentStatus reads one component's state in every environment it declares,
// from a checkout already on disk. Status without the session, the ArgoCD call
// or the report: no lock, no network, no output. Nothing here fails — an
// unreadable environment comes back Onboarded false with a Reason.
func ComponentStatus(ctx context.Context, root string, g *git.Client,
    deployCfg *gitops.DeployConfig, coord gitops.Coordinate,
    comp *gitops.ComponentConfig) StatusResult
```

Body is `:52-60` plus the `StatusResult` assembly from `reportStatus` (`:244-251`).
`Status()` becomes session → `locateComponent` → `ComponentStatus` →
`observeArgo` → `reportStatus`. `statusEnvironments` (`:77`), `readOverlayState`,
`consistent` (`:222`) and `pinSignature` (`:202`) are all reused, none duplicated.

**The refactor is done when every existing test in `internal/deploy` passes
unedited.** That is the "CLI behaves identically" assertion — do not weaken it.

### 3. Serve the prose; do not re-derive it in TypeScript

`summarise` (`:352`) and `notes` (`:435`) are the honesty layer of this whole
feature — the sentences that separate *"these two run different bits"* from
*"there is nothing to compare here"*, and that explain an empty digest for a
`kind: shared` component. The Go tests assert on that prose. Reimplementing it in
React is the single most likely way this feature becomes dishonest, because two
implementations means two conclusions from one set of rows and only one of them is
tested.

Two additive fields, which `StatusResult`'s own doc licenses ("field names are
stable and additive-only"):

```go
// Summary and Notes are the sentences the plain table prints beneath itself:
// what the environments collectively run, and the qualifications — what could
// not be read, what pins a tag, what is waiting. They travel in the result so a
// second presenter cannot draw a different conclusion from the same rows.
Summary string   `json:"summary"`
Notes   []string `json:"notes,omitempty"`
```

`ComponentStatus` fills them via the existing functions; `reportStatus` reads them
back off the result so there is one call site. **This additively changes
`deploy status -o json`** — it gains prose the plain output already showed. That is
an improvement, and it is the recommendation; the alternative (a dashboard-local
wrapper struct) means two structs asserting the same claim.

### 4. `internal/deploy/survey.go` (new) — every component, one pass, no lock

```go
type SurveyOptions struct {
    // Root is a checkout already on disk. Survey never clones, fetches or
    // locks: the caller either owns a session or, like the dashboard, is
    // reading what an earlier command left behind.
    Root string

    // Git reads each overlay's last-changed commit, which is what dates a
    // deployment. Nil skips it.
    Git *git.Client

    // Coords narrows the survey. Empty means every component in the tree.
    Coords []gitops.Coordinate
}

// SurveyEntry is one component's state, or the reason it has none.
type SurveyEntry struct {
    Coordinate gitops.Coordinate
    Status     *StatusResult

    // Error is why this component could not be described — an unreadable or
    // invalid component.yaml. Status is then nil. One malformed component never
    // costs the caller the rest of the tree.
    Error string
}

// Survey reads every component's state from one checkout. N calls to Status
// would take the exclusive lock N times, fetch N times, and could only hand
// back rendered text.
func Survey(ctx context.Context, opts SurveyOptions) (*gitops.DeployConfig, []SurveyEntry, []string)
```

Implementation: `gitops.ListComponents(root)` — one glob, `layout.go:142` — →
`LoadComponentConfig` → `ComponentStatus`, in the order `ListComponents` returns.

Cost with `Git` set is one `git log -1 -- <path>` per component per environment:
roughly a second for 30 components × 3 envs on a warm repo. Acceptable behind the
lazy cache, which today already fronts a `dotnet build`. If measurement later
demands it, a single `git log --name-only --format` pass over `domains/` replaces
the loop.

### 5. `internal/dashboard/deploy.go` (new) — provider and join

Mirrors `topology.go`, for the reason it already states (`:23`): *"The mechanics
live in topology.RunGraph… What stays here is the dashboard's policy."* `gitops`
and `deploy` stay ignorant of the workspace identifier space.

```go
// deployProvider surveys the GitOps repository. Like topologyProvider it never
// fails: an unconfigured repository, an absent checkout or an unreadable one
// each come back as a Source state, because "we do not know" and "it is not
// deployed" must never render the same.
type deployProvider func(ctx context.Context, opts refreshOptions) deploySurvey

// refreshOptions is what a refresh is allowed to do beyond re-reading the
// cache. The zero value is a pure local read, which is what a GET always gets.
type refreshOptions struct {
    Fetch  bool // take the lock and fetch from the remote
    Argocd bool // read sync and health
}
```

**The join.** The codebase states the rule twice — `init.go:493` (*"the source
workspace's own layout, which every customer integrations tree mirrors from the
deployment tree"*) and `initmodel.go:134` `matchScaffolds` (*"a component's
directory basename, and its scaffold record's `values.appId`. Both are matched —
directory first"*). Follow the established convention rather than invent one. First
hit wins:

| # | `matchedBy` | rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | `coordinate` | `{Domain, System, Name}` == `{c.Domain, c.System, c.Component}`, exactly one hit |
| 2 | `system` | integration has no domain: `{System, Name}` matches, exactly one hit |
| 3 | `appId` | `values.appId == c.Component` **and** `System == c.System`, exactly one hit |

Case-folded, to match `sys create`'s kebab-casing.

**There is deliberately no bare-name rule.** Per memory, component names collide
across customers and `config.yaml` is a single flat `gitopsRepo`;
`gitops.AmbiguousComponentError` (`layout.go:53`) exists precisely because a name
occurs in several places. Matching on name alone would attribute another system's
production digest to this integration — the worst failure available here, and it
must be structurally impossible rather than merely unlikely.

Outcomes: one hit → `matched:true` + `matchedBy` + `status`; no hit → `matched:false`
with a reason naming same-named components at other coordinates as `candidates`, so
a mislaid domain reads as a mislaid domain; more than one hit → `matched:false`,
both `candidates`, and **`status: nil`** — never resolved by picking one. GitOps
components no integration claims go in `orphans`, because a deployed workload
nobody accounts for is a finding, not noise.

### 6. `internal/dashboard/handlers.go` — wire it

`newHandler`'s parameter list is about to grow, so collapse it once:

```go
type providers struct {
    topology topologyProvider
    deploy   deployProvider
}

func newHandler(root, version string, p providers) (http.Handler, error)
```

Cache state on `apiServer` mirrors `topoMu/topoLoaded/topoEntries/topoErrs`
(`:32-35`) field for field; the accessor mirrors `cachedTopologies` (`:258-271`).
Two routes beside the topology pair (`:99-100`):

```go
mux.HandleFunc("GET /api/deploy", api.deployState)          // always refreshOptions{}
mux.HandleFunc("POST /api/deploy/refresh", api.refreshDeploy) // Fetch+Argocd
```

Payload:

```go
type deployReport struct {
    // Source says where this came from and how current it is. Always present,
    // including when nothing could be read — it is what keeps "no GitOps
    // repository is configured" from rendering as "not deployed".
    Source deploySource `json:"source"`

    // Integrations covers every catalogued integration, keyed by the same
    // root-relative path /api/integrations uses. Always an array; an unmatched
    // integration is present and says why.
```
